note: Offline gates of the motor assist version 2 (configs/pilot/motor_assist.json), scored by haltere.liftoff.motor_assist_gates (score). Frozen with the rule version, after its design on development sets only (the declaration's development_results) and before any run of the held-out parts below. Every scenario and course gate compares the assist with the baseline on the same scenarios, courses, drones and surrogate: the baseline is the m4b pilot as the runner builds it for the motor contract (--looming-brake --obstacle-stack on --descent-view on: lag turn v2, gap pilot v5 without gap samples, wall pilot v5, vertical guard v4, descent view v2 with contact support) without the assist. The hairpin and pass-through sets and the hill seeds are new and disjoint from every development set; the replay gates use the live logs, of which the Minus Two brain logs minus-brain03-01 ... minus-brain08-slow35-01 and the Straw Bale lap straw-brain11cw13-r4b-noassist-02 were never replayed through any version of the assist (held out) and the rest are development cases (named). The surrogate is development evidence, never flight evidence: no Liftoff walls, terrain, contact physics or HUD rules, synthetic looming. The hash covers everything except frozen/frozen_at/sha256; each gate is scored once per rule version. Version 1 of these gates (motor_assist_gates_v1.json) is kept.
baseline: the m4b pilot (2a5bccb) for the motor contract without the motor assist: bit-identical to this tree with the assist off (the identity gate)

surrogate.loop: descent_rehearsal.run_batch (dev16, hill) and motor_assist_eval.run_scenarios (hairpin, accelerate): IdentifiedSim with 10% per-drone randomisation, synthetic HUD marker (camera period 0.055 s, latency 0.06 s, 10% dropout), 3-tick command delay, quadratic drag 0.0075, 1 s arming hold; run_scenarios adds synthetic looming of the scenario wall (18 Hz, received 0.085 s after capture, the horizontal travel ray within 20 m and 55 deg of the heading) and a 1.5 m checkpoint radius; the pass-through scenarios add a looming-only surface at the arch that reads clear within see_through_m and beyond it

brain11cw13.use: fast-brain-11-b-cw13 (the best-ranked brain-11 candidate, flown in round 4b live)

brain09b.use: the brain-09b development candidate (flown in rounds 3-4 as a disclosed deviation)

brain10b.use: the fast-brain-10b candidate (not selected by its gates; flown in round 4 as a disclosed deviation)

course_sets.definitions: descent_rehearsal.course_set: hill = hill_course(seed) with hills (the descent gates' kind; seeds 6300-6311 are new: the descent gates and version 1 used 6000-6011)

hairpin.definition: motor_assist_eval.hairpin_scenario for every combination (12), as version 1 defines it (from the ground, north 20 m to R1, a right turn of turn_deg to the arch R2 arch_m further, a wall wall_m behind R2 across that leg (12 m wide), R3 6 m to the left and 1 m before the wall, R4 15 m further left; rings 0.8 m high, a 2.2 m ceiling, the marker lost for 0.45 s after R2). Development sets (not scored): turn 20/60/90 and 45/75/105 deg, arch 7/11 and 8/13 m, wall 2.1/2.6 and 2.3/3.0 m, seeds 17 and 23

passthrough.definition: REPORT, not a gate: motor_assist_eval.passthrough_scenario for every combination (8): a gate arch flown through with a looming-only surface surface_m beyond the ring, read until see_through_m, clear beyond; the lowest horizontal speed from 1.5 s before to 0.5 s after the arch pass. Development (pt17: turn 0/45/90, see-through 1/2 m, seed 17) showed that the governor's own stand-off holds a slowed brain near 1 m/s there, and the fast PD dips too although it passes these Minus arches live at 3.5-4 m/s, so the scenario's looming is not validated against Liftoff

windows.what: the hairpin approach to 0.05 s before the wall impact
the hairpin approach to 0.05 s before the wall impact (version 1's window)
the hairpin approach to the turn-first stop

windows.definition: REPORT, not a gate (DEVELOPMENT cases): motor_assist_eval.live_window, the logged state at t0 in the surrogate, the brain warmed on the recorded inputs; the pilot's own request from an open-loop replay of the log through this tree's stack and, with the assist, the assisted request from the surrogate's measured velocity with the binding caps and the wall-ahead condition the pilot had at each logged state (the sources come from the logged positions: a surrogate drone that slows falls behind them, so the later bounds are conservative)

replays.variants: this tree: vertical_replay --stack on --near-on-path --throttle-column command_thr --descent-view configs/pilot/descent_view.json [--motor-assist configs/pilot/motor_assist.json | configs/pilot/motor_assist_v1.json] and --stack none; the baseline tree the same without the assist and with its configs/pilot/motor_assist.json (version 1); the looming streams for the stream flights

gates.identity: every pair bit-identical on the COMMAND_KEYS of haltere.obstacles.vertical_replay

definitions.hairpin: per brain over the 12 held-out hairpins. A contact is the drone centre within 0.3 m of the wall plane, below 0.05 m after the first ring, above the ceiling - 0.1 m, or a surrogate crash; a clean pass finishes all four rings with none. Clean passes >= the baseline's + 6; wall contacts <= floor(25% of the baseline's); floor contacts <= the baseline's + 1; ceiling contacts <= the baseline's + 1 (the contact-support false fire of about 2 of 12 drones is in both)
definitions.hill: per brain over the 12 held-out hill courses (the Straw-like closed loop; no looming there, so the stopping model is idle and this checks the rest of the rule): finishes >= the baseline's; crashes <= the baseline's; mean stick chatter <= 1.15 x; mean finish time over the courses both finish <= 1.02 x (the proposed course-time bound); terrain contacts <= the baseline's + 1; passes > 1.5 m high <= the baseline's + 2
definitions.minus_plan: open loop, every Minus Two brain log (development and held-out): no planned stop or crawl before the hairpin: no run of >= 0.1 s, before the logged drone first reaches x = 73 m, in which the stopping model's bound (assist_plan: approach or stopping) is below 2.0 m/s while the pilot's own horizontal request is at least 3.0 m/s (the first arch, pillar A and the 90-degree arch lie before x = 73 m). Offline scoring uses the logged position; the rule does not
definitions.warning: open loop, DEVELOPMENT cases (the two brain logs that hit the hairpin wall): the time before the logged impact (the log's end) at which the assisted horizontal request first falls 1.0 m/s or more below the pilot's own, within the last 3 s; >= 1.0 s (the governor's cap dropped 0.72 s before the impact on minus-brain11cw13-r4b-noassist-01)
definitions.quiet: open loop, every Straw Bale and Pine Valley brain lap with looming samples (development and held-out): the stopping source (a wall-ahead condition) is the source that removed the most on <= 0.5 s per minute; the horizontal request travel removed on ticks attributed to the stopping model (approach or stopping) <= 2% of the pilot's own request travel (an upper bound of the course time lost: the recorded drone does not slow); by every source <= 3% (version 1's quiet bound); no more turn-first episodes than without the assist
definitions.slew: every brain replay with the assist: on every tick with dt > 1e-4 s, the change of (assisted - own) is at most 15 m/s^2 x dt horizontally (vector norm) and vertically (+1e-6)
definitions.identity: (a) the pilot with the assist off (the full stack and the default pilot) on this tree equals the baseline tree on every identity flight; (b) the fast PD with --motor-assist on (version 2) equals it off; (c) the kept version-1 declaration replayed through this tree equals the baseline tree's version 1 on the brain logs

reported_not_gated: the pass-through arches, the live windows, floor/ceiling details, chatter on the scenario sets, the approach seconds per minute, the per-log assisted request minima (open-loop cap tracking dips while the recorded drone does not slow)
scope: measured surrogate (IdentifiedSim) on seeded synthetic scenarios and courses, and open-loop replays of live logs; development evidence, not flight evidence
